en: Ice cubes float in a glass of water because solid water is less dense than liquid water.
Iron gates turn reddish-brown when exposed to oxygen and moisture in the humid Philippine air.
Evaporating seawater from Manila Bay leaves behind solid salt crystals, separating the mixture into its components.
Solid tablea chocolate melts into a liquid when stirred into hot water to make tsokolate.
Water vapor condenses into tiny liquid droplets to form the white clouds seen above Mount Makiling.
Metal roofs of local houses expand and creak when heated by the strong tropical afternoon sun.
Muddy water from the Pasig River is a heterogeneous mixture where solid dirt particles settle at the bottom.
Burning dried mango leaves produces ash and smoke, demonstrating a chemical change that creates new substances.
Black iron sand on the beaches of Ilocos is strongly attracted to a magnet due to its metallic properties.
Solid mothballs in a wooden cabinet slowly turn directly into a gas through a process called sublimation.
Granulated sugar dissolves completely in liquid calamansi juice to form a clear, sweet, homogeneous solution.
Crushing solid pumice rocks from Taal Volcano into smaller pieces is a physical change that does not alter their chemical composition.
